The APM plays a key role in ensuring project success through accurate documentation, communication, and coordination across the project team, subcontractors, and owners. Resolve complex project issues and discrepancies in plans, schedules, and documents. Conduct weekly job meetings; document and distribute clear meeting minutes. Expedite and manage material deliveries, shop drawings, submittals, RFIs, and change order logs. Prepare addenda, plan revisions, and Owner update reports. Capture and organize project progress photos. Support timely and accurate project closeout documentation. Demonstrate strong skills in reading plans, performing quantity takeoffs, and identifying discrepancies. Project Accounting & Budget Management Draft purchase orders, subcontracts, and change orders. Review and approve vendor and subcontractor invoices with accuracy. Maintain the job cost report and track overall project budget. Prepare monthly Owner applications for payment and supporting documentation. Track and document all change orders and budget impacts. Submit all accounting documents to the Project Manager for approval. Train less experienced Assistant Project Managers in project accounting processes. Demonstrate a strong working knowledge of construction accounting practices. Estimating & Preconstruction Support Perform preliminary job pricing and justify estimating approaches. Prepare solicitation lists for subcontractors and suppliers. Develop bid packages and manage bid solicitation. Tabulate and evaluate bids for accuracy and completeness. Perform quantity surveys and initial estimate pricing. Apply strong mathematical skills (geometry, basic algebra) to estimating tasks. Mentor and train junior Assistant Project Managers. Work independently with minimal supervision while balancing multiple priorities. Negotiate and help resolve complex project issues and subcontractor challenges. Assist with company marketing activities when requested. Software & Technology Utilize computers and construction‑related software effectively (e.g., Primavera, Timberline, scheduling tools). Maintain accurate digital documentation including logs, reports, schedules, and correspondence. Advanced Duties Act as Project Manager on small, low‑risk projects under guidance of the VP of Operations. Support business development and marketing assignments when needed. Perform additional duties as assigned to support overall project and company success. Qualifications Qualifications, Education & Experience 2-5 years total construction experience. Experience may include roles such as Project Engineer, Field Engineer, Intern, Project Coordinator, or entry-level APM. Exposure to commercial construction processes, RFIs, submittals, scheduling basics, and document control. Education & Experience Bachelor’s degree in construction management, Engineering, Architecture or related field OR equivalent construction experience.
